title: The agriculture orientation index for government expenditures
graph_title: The agriculture orientation index for government expenditures
national_indicator_available: Agriculture orientation index for government expenditures
national_indicator_description: An Agriculture Orientation Index (AOI) greater than 1 reflects a higher orientation towards the agriculture sector, which receives a higher share of government spending relative to its contribution to economic value-added. An AOI less than 1 reflects a lower orientation to agriculture, while an AOI equal to 1 reflects neutrality in a government's orientation to the agriculture sector. The numerator and denominator are also provided here as separate series.
computation_definitions: The agriculture orientation index for government expenditures is defined as the agriculture share of government expenditure, divided by the agriculture value added share of GDP.
computation_calculations:
First, the numerator and denominator are calculated separately.

The agriculture share of government expenditure is calculated as - Budget allocated to the relevant sector / Total budget * 100.

The agriculture value added share of GDP is calculated as - Agriculture value added / Total GDP * 100.

Finally, the agriculture orientation index for government expenditures is calculated as - Agriculture share of government expenditure / Agriculture value added share of GDP.
comments_limitations: The agriculture orientation index itself was calculated specifically for this indicator based on public data. As the numerator and denominator come from different sources, there may be differences in methodology; please see the linked data source for more information.
indicator_name: The agriculture orientation index for government expenditures
target_name: Increase investment, including through enhanced international cooperation, in rural infrastructure, agricultural research and extension services, technology development and plant and livestock gene banks in order to enhance agricultural productive capacity in developing countries, in particular least developed countries
indicator_definition: The Agriculture Orientation Index (AOI) for Government Expenditures is defined as the Agriculture share of Government Expenditure, divided by the Agriculture value added share of GDP, where Agriculture refers to the agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting sector. The measure is a currency-free index, calculated as the ratio of these two shares. National governments are requested to compile Government Expenditures according to the Government Finance Statistics (GFS) and the Classification of the Functions of Government (COFOG), and Agriculture value added share of GDP according to the System of National Accounts (SNA).

source_other_info_1: This is the source for the series "Agriculture value added share of GDP", which is also the denominator used to calculate the Agriculture Orientation Index (AOI) for Government Expenditures.
source_organisation_2: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN)
source_other_info_2: This is the source for the series "Agriculture share of government expenditure", which is also the numerator used to calculate the Agriculture Orientation Index (AOI) for Government Expenditures. For each calendar year, the revised finance law for the fiscal year ending in that calendar year is used, except for 2009, for which the mini budget is used due to Rwanda joining the East African Community Customs Union (EAC) and subsequently changing from the calendar year to a July/June fiscal year on 1st of July 2009. Prior to 2010/11, the relevant breakdowns can be found in Annex II-1, "Budget by Sector" (prior to 2008; file name is "Functional") or "State Expenditure per Sector and Sub-Sector" (2008 onwards). For 2010/2011 and 2011/2012, the relevant breakdowns can be found in Annex II-4, "State Expenditure by Sector and Sub-Sector". From 2011/2012 onwards, the relevant breakdowns can be found in Annex II-8, "State Expenditure by Division and Groups" (prior to 2019/2020) or "State Expenditure by COFOG Divisions and Groups" (2019/2020 onwards).
